symptoms: payments-api returned 5xx error rate above 38% for 23 minutes after v2.4.1 deploy
log_snippet: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
root_cause: database connection pool exhausted because the new release opened a connection per request without releasing
actions_tried: restarted pods (no effect, connections immediately maxed out)
rolled back to v2.4.0 (resolved in 4 minutes)
resolution: rolled back to v2.4.0, error rate dropped to 0%
permanent_fix: increased max pool size from 20 to 50 and fixed the connection leak in DB transaction wrapper

symptoms: orders-api 5xx after new v2.4.1 deploy, checkout queues backing up
log_snippet: Timeout acquiring DB connection after 30000ms in HikariPool-1
root_cause: same connection pool leak pattern introduced in shared database client library v2.4.1
actions_tried: restarted pods (connections re-exhausted within 90 seconds)
rolled back release to v2.4.0 (resolved)
resolution: rollback fixed the issue in 5 minutes
permanent_fix: upgraded shared db-client to v2.4.2 containing pooled connection fix

symptoms: orders-api connection timeouts and 503 errors during flash sale
log_snippet: java.sql.SQLTransientConnectionException: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
root_cause: connection pool size was set to default 10, unable to handle 4x baseline traffic
actions_tried: scaled replicas from 3 to 10 (caused postgres max_connections limit error)
rolled back replica scale, bumped pool size to 35
resolution: increased pool size to 35 per pod and tuned postgres max_connections to 300
permanent_fix: added dynamic connection pool autoscaling and PgBouncer connection pooler

symptoms: checkout-service p99 latency spiked to 28s, 504 gateway timeouts
log_snippet: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available (total=30, active=30, idle=0, waiting=95)
root_cause: unindexed query in newly deployed promo-code validator held connections open for 15s each
actions_tried: scaling replicas (made pool problem worse, exhausted db slots)
disabled promo-code feature flag (immediate recovery)
resolution: disabled promo-code feature flag via consul
permanent_fix: added composite index on promo_codes(code, active_from, active_to)

symptoms: intermittent payment capture timeouts and database connection refused
log_snippet: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
root_cause: stray migration script left 120 idle connections in transaction state on postgres-primary
actions_tried: restarted payments-api (no effect, DB slots still occupied)
terminated idle backend connections via pg_terminate_backend
resolution: terminated idle backend processes older than 30 minutes in postgres
permanent_fix: configured idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 60000ms in postgresql.conf

symptoms: 100% of external API clients failing with SSL handshake errors
log_snippet: SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:0A000086:SSL routines::certificate verify failed) certificate has expired
root_cause: Let's Encrypt wildcard certificate expired at midnight UTC because auto-renewal cronjob was disabled during cluster upgrade
actions_tried: restarted envoy proxy on api-gateway (cert still expired)
manually triggered cert-manager renewal and secret reload
resolution: renewed certificate via cert-manager CLI and restarted ingress pods to pick up new secret
permanent_fix: added Prometheus alert at 30, 14, and 7 days before TLS expiry

symptoms: user logins and OAuth token issuance failing with certificate validation errors
log_snippet: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2026-09-27T08:15:22Z is after 2026-09-27T08:00:00Z
root_cause: internal mTLS certificate for auth-service expired; cert-manager renewal was blocked by DNS challenge failure
actions_tried: bypassed mTLS temporarily (rejected by security policy)
fixed Route53 DNS challenge IAM permissions and re-triggered cert-manager
resolution: granted route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets to cert-manager IAM role and force-renewed
permanent_fix: automated cert-manager DNS-01 challenge healthchecks in CI/CD pipeline

symptoms: webhook deliveries from payment partners failing with TLS peer verification failed
log_snippet: curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
root_cause: intermediate CA certificate bundle missing in updated api-gateway config
actions_tried: restarted api-gateway pods (no change)
appended intermediate certificate to fullchain.pem
resolution: re-uploaded fullchain certificate with complete trust chain to Kubernetes secrets
permanent_fix: enforced fullchain linting in Terraform SSL secret deployment module

symptoms: bank payout integration dropped to 0 transactions, handshake failure reported
log_snippet: javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: Received fatal alert: certificate_expired
root_cause: partner banking client certificate expired on our outbound egress proxy
actions_tried: restarted egress proxy (no effect)
retrieved new client certificate from partner portal and updated secret
resolution: installed newly issued client certificate in egress keystore
permanent_fix: established quarterly certificate audit schedule with all financial partners

symptoms: postgres-primary disk at 99%, all database write transactions failing with disk full
log_snippet: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device; HINT: Check free disk space.
root_cause: abandoned replication slot 'analytics_replica_old' prevented postgres from removing pg_wal log segments
actions_tried: deleted old log files in /tmp (freed only 200MB)
dropped unused replication slot analytics_replica_old (freed 85GB instantly)
resolution: dropped the dead replication slot and reclaimed 85GB of WAL storage
permanent_fix: set max_slot_wal_keep_size = 20GB to prevent replication slots from filling disks

symptoms: logging aggregator stopped receiving traces; elasticsearch indices in read-only mode
log_snippet: disk_threshold_decider: [logging-node-01] flood-stage disk watermark [95%] exceeded on high disk watermark [90%]
root_cause: debug logging was accidentally enabled in production payments-api, generating 50GB logs in 3 hours
actions_tried: restarted elasticsearch service (failed to start due to disk lock)
deleted indices older than 14 days and reverted log level to INFO
resolution: reverted log level to INFO and purged indices older than 14 days
permanent_fix: configured Curator to automatically purge indices when disk reaches 85%

symptoms: system logs buffer overflow, disk usage at 100% on root partition
log_snippet: systemd-journald[512]: Failed to write entry to /var/log/journal: No space left on device
root_cause: logrotate cronjob stopped running due to bad file permissions on /etc/cron.daily/logrotate
actions_tried: cleared apt cache (freed 1GB temporarily)
fixed logrotate permissions (chmod +x) and ran logrotate -f
resolution: forced logrotate execution and compressed historical system logs
permanent_fix: enforced file permissions via Ansible configuration management playbook

symptoms: read-replica lag jumped to 6 hours, primary disk alarm triggered at 94%
log_snippet: archive_command: cp: error writing '/mnt/nfs/wal_archive/0000000100000': No space left on device
root_cause: NFS mount for WAL archiving became read-only after storage server disk filled
actions_tried: stopped archive_command (risked backup loss)
expanded NFS volume on storage server and remounted rw
resolution: expanded NFS volume by 500GB, archive_command resumed and cleared backlog
permanent_fix: migrated WAL archiving from NFS to AWS S3 using wal-g

symptoms: checkout-service p99 latency spike to 12s, cache hit ratio plummeted from 94% to 12%
log_snippet: WARN CartCache miss ratio 0.66 falling back to postgres; RedisCommandTimeoutException: Command timed out after 2 second(s)
root_cause: Redis eviction storm: maxmemory was set to 4GB with volatile-lru policy, key TTLs expired simultaneously
actions_tried: scaled checkout-service replicas (overwhelmed postgres with cache-miss queries)
increased Redis maxmemory to 8GB and switched eviction policy to allkeys-lru
resolution: increased Redis maxmemory to 8GB and changed policy to allkeys-lru
permanent_fix: added jitter to cache TTLs (300s +/- 45s) to eliminate synchronized mass expiration

symptoms: orders-api unable to write new orders to cache, returning 500 internal server error
log_snippet: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'. Command: SET order:state:98231
root_cause: new feature wrote uncompressed customer tracking payloads to redis without setting an expiration TTL
actions_tried: restarted redis-cache (lost in-flight session data)
flushed keys matching order:tracking:* and deployed hotfix with 1hr TTL
resolution: purged unexpired tracking keys using redis-cli scan and unlink
permanent_fix: implemented CI linter that fails if redis SET commands lack EX/PX expiry argument

symptoms: checkout cart service experiencing intermittent connection dropouts and latency spikes
log_snippet: Redis error: Slow query detected: KEYS cart:* took 4200ms
root_cause: admin diagnostic tool executed KEYS pattern search in production Redis instead of SCAN
actions_tried: restarted redis (rejected to avoid dropping cache)
killed the running KEYS query process using CLIENT KILL
resolution: killed rogue admin connection via redis-cli client kill
permanent_fix: renamed and disabled the KEYS command in redis.conf using rename-command KEYS ''

symptoms: Redis CPU utilization pinned at 100%, read/write commands timing out across all services
log_snippet: JedisConnectionException: Unexpected end of stream; Redis INFO: instantaneous_ops_per_sec: 145000
root_cause: marketing push notification triggered simultaneous session lookup storm for 200,000 active users
actions_tried: restarted redis instance (made outage worse, backend crashed)
enabled local memory caching (Caffeine) in checkout-service with 30s TTL
resolution: deployed multi-tier caching with in-memory Caffeine cache to absorb hot read keys
permanent_fix: scaled Redis to a 3-node Redis Cluster with read replicas

symptoms: auth-service returning 401 Unauthorized and 429 Too Many Requests to valid logged-in users
